subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Water Chemistry
description: A quick win: understand Water Chemistry.

hook.text: Coffee is 98% water. If your water tastes bad, your coffee will taste bad—no matter how good the beans are.

buildup.text: Mineral content matters. Calcium and magnesium help extract flavor compounds from coffee grounds.

discovery.text: The Specialty Coffee Association recommends 75–250 ppm total dissolved solids for optimal brewing.

twist.text: Distilled water tastes flat because it lacks minerals to bind with coffee's flavor molecules.

climax.text: Competition baristas custom-build water with precise mineral recipes to maximize extraction quality.

punchline.text: Perfect beans, wrong water, ruined cup. Water is the recipe.

quiz.question: Why does distilled water make poor coffee?
options: It lacks minerals needed to extract flavor compounds
